title: Association between physical activity intensity and self-reported emphysema: A cross-sectional study using NHANES
content:
by Qiao Wei, Haiyan Song, Li Jiang, Xiuqin Li, Jihua Zhu

Background

Emphysema is a significant public health issue. Physical activity (PA) has been suggested to be associated with respiratory health; however, the relationship between PA intensity and emphysema remains insufficiently characterized.

Methods

This cross-sectional study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007 to 2016. Emphysema was defined based on self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association between different levels of PA and the odds of self-reported emphysema among older adults, adjusting for demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities.

Results

Higher levels of physical activity, particularly ≥3000 MET-minutes per week, were associated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema. A dose–response relationship was observed, with increasing PA levels associated with progressively lower odds of self-reported emphysema.

Conclusions

Higher physical activity levels were associated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema in this cross-sectional analysis. These findings highlight a potential association between PA and self-reported emphysema; however, causal inference cannot be established. Prospective studies are warranted to further evaluate this relationship and explore underlying mechanisms.
author: Qiao Wei
